reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not mention electrospark deposition, Al additions, or coating performance on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr. E1 only notes that anti-oxidation coatings are required, and E2 describes powder processing, providing no support for the key premises.
premises: Electrospark deposition can produce an ultrathin, dense anti-oxidation coating on refractory alloys.
A minor Al addition promotes formation of a protective Al₂O₃ scale on HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will form a continuous, adherent oxide scale that significantly reduces oxygen uptake.
The coating will not degrade the alloy's room-temperature ductility or high-temperature yield strength.
The protective effect is valid for 5 h at 800 °C in air under static and cyclic loading.
